source: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1 (CC BY 4.0), Ch. 5-6

concepts.name: Vectors and components
concepts.description: Represent a quantity with magnitude and direction; resolve into x/y components.

concepts.name: Velocity and acceleration
concepts.description: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity; constant velocity means zero acceleration.

concepts.name: Mass and inertia
concepts.description: Mass measures resistance to changes in motion.

concepts.name: Force as interaction
concepts.description: A force is a push or pull from one object on another, with magnitude and direction.

concepts.name: Net force
concepts.description: Forces on one object add as vectors; only the sum determines acceleration.

concepts.name: Free-body diagrams
concepts.description: Isolate one object and draw only the forces acting ON it.

concepts.name: Newton's first law
concepts.description: With zero net force, velocity stays constant; no force is needed to keep moving.

concepts.name: Newton's second law
concepts.description: Net force equals mass times acceleration, as a vector equation.

concepts.name: Weight vs. mass
concepts.description: Weight is the gravitational force mg; mass is intrinsic and does not change with location.

concepts.name: Newton's third law
concepts.description: Forces come in equal-and-opposite pairs acting on DIFFERENT objects.

concepts.name: Normal force
concepts.description: A surface pushes perpendicular to itself, just enough to prevent penetration; not always equal to mg.

concepts.name: Tension
concepts.description: A taut rope transmits a pulling force along its length.

concepts.name: Friction
concepts.description: Static and kinetic friction oppose relative sliding, scaling with the normal force.

concepts.name: Inclined planes
concepts.description: Resolve weight into components parallel and perpendicular to the surface.
